ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Given: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AD$ is the altitude on side $BC$. There is an inscribed rectangle $PQMN$ within the triangle, with one side of the rectangle on $BC$, and the other two vertices on $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. If $BC=60$ and $AD=40$, what is the length of $PQ$ when $PQ=PN$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral PQMN is a rectangle,\\
it follows that PQ$\parallel$BC,\\
which implies $\triangle APQ\sim \triangle ABC$,\\
also, since AD$\perp$BC,\\
this leads to AE$\perp$PQ,\\
thus, quadrilateral PEDN forms a rectangle,\\
resulting in PN=DE,\\
from $\triangle APQ\sim \triangle ABC$ we get $ \frac{PQ}{BC}=\frac{AE}{AD}$,\\
since PQ=PN,\\
it follows that $ \frac{PQ}{60}=\frac{40-PQ}{40}$,\\
solving this yields PQ$=\boxed{24}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Solution: Since quadrilateral $PQMN$ is a rectangle, $PQ\parallel BC$, which implies $\triangle APQ\sim \triangle ABC$. Also, since $AD\perp BC$, this leads to $AE\perp PQ$, thus quadrilateral $PEDN$ forms a rectangle, resulting in $PN=DE$. From $\triangle APQ\sim \triangle ABC$ we get $\frac{PQ}{BC}=\frac{AE}{AD}$. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, with BC as the horizontal base, and A above; AD drops perpendicularly from A to D on BC. Rectangle PQMN is inscribed in the triangle, N and M are on BC, P is on AB, Q is on AC, PQ is the upper side of the rectangle and is parallel to BC; AD intersects PQ at E. Reasoning: Let x = PQ. The problem gives PQ = PN, so the height PN of the rectangle is also equal to x. Since AD = 40, and the vertical distance from BC to PQ is equal to the rectangle height x, the distance from A to PQ is AE = 40 - x. Because PQ ∥ BC, triangle APQ and triangle ABC are similar. Corresponding sides are proportional: PQ/BC = AE/AD. Substituting BC = 60 and AD = 40 gives x/60 = (40 - x)/40. Solve the equation: 40x = 60(40 - x) = 2400 - 60x, so 100x = 2400, x = 24. Therefore PQ = 24.
